PullRequest.Title: agentHost: add correlated startup performance telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Add bounded, content-free `agentHost.startupMark` telemetry to diagnose startup regressions and compare workloads such as fewer than 100 versus more than 100 Copilot sessions.

- Correlate bootstrap, readiness, listing, migration, and provider enumeration with one UUID per Agent Host process lifetime.
- Record provider session counts, catalog/fallback and storage metrics, migration/backfill state, provider registration, and first-access activation/SDK availability.
- Observe the actual first successful listing and startup-settled barrier independently of concurrent sampled listings and the three-attempt sampling cap.
- Reuse existing enumeration and availability decisions; add no telemetry-triggered scans, database reads, SDK probes, downloads, timers, or awaited flushes. Preserve usage-telemetry consent and local trace logging.
- Document the [startup graph and measurement contract](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/e6efbce589490598329b6dce80bc981421d52077/src/vs/platform/agentHost/PERFORMANCE.md).

## Measurement boundaries

Cumulative readiness milestones can include waiting for the first client request; they are distinct from client-perceived startup latency. Provider scans may overlap or run after startup and stop before filtering/publication. Missing context/counts remain unknown rather than zero. Operation sampling remains capped; early failures before telemetry publication are not a complete launch denominator.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`: passed with zero errors.
- Targeted startup, session aggregation, migration, and provider-gating regressions: **447 passing, 11 pending**.
- Client typecheck and targeted ESLint passed.
- All **40 telemetry fields**, including **30 numeric/boolean measurements**, checked for classification and optionality.
- Markdown links/code fences and patch whitespace checked.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold Agent Host process bootstrap through service construction and host-ready publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration and the existing telemetry service must initialize before core services are constructed. The diff adds fixed-count in-memory clock/Map work and synchronous telemetry-pipeline enqueueing at named milestones; it adds no awaited flush, network response, filesystem read, database read, IPC, or subprocess startup to readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pass each startup marker to the existing ITelemetryService/1DS appender pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed set of bootstrap/host milestones per process lifetime; each milestone is deduplicated by name/provider, rather than scaling with sessions or requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No startup-marker events were enqueued; the existing telemetry service and appenders were still initialized during bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local enqueue/serialization call is synchronous, but delivery is not awaited and remote completion is off the startup critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed milestone count per Agent Host process, independent of session count and client count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Bootstrap milestones are serialized by process initialization. No new task fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentHostStartupMarks buffers only the fixed pre-telemetry milestones, drains them once, and deduplicates repeated milestones. Consent-disabled operations are not replayed after opt-in.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, mark, deduplication, and publicLog2 call paths were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender-internal serialization cost varies by telemetry backend, but event count and payload size are strictly bounded and delivery is not awaited.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new startup work is fixed-size and does not add an awaited expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: First and sampled aggregate session listings, including concurrent callers and registry refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing list must read registrations, optionally bulk-read the catalog, resolve bounded provider/session fallbacks, overlay live state, and filter visibility before returning. The diff adds one provider-count pass over the already-materialized registration array and bounded telemetry markers; it does not add database or provider reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read registered sessions and central catalog rows, with existing per-session fallback reads where catalog entries are ineligible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped registration/catalog read per coalesced list computation; fallback resolution remains limited to four concurrent rows and is proportional only to effective catalog misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same registration, bulk catalog, and fallback reads occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing reads remain on the list response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask each fallback-capable provider for one shared metadata prewarm before per-row fallback resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one prewarm per provider represented among effective fallback rows; Copilot retains its threshold, TTL cache, and in-flight coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped provider prewarm occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prewarm remains awaited before fallback rows resolve.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue bounded start/end and first-list telemetry records through the existing telemetry pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three sampled attempts for host sessionList plus one firstSessionList milestone per process; overlapping same-mode callers share one computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No startup-list telemetry events were emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion callbacks run locally after computation settles; telemetry delivery is not awaited by listSessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Registered session count after one grouped registry read; telemetry adds one O(n) integer-count pass only for the bounded startup observations, while existing list work already performs multiple O(n) transforms and potentially much more expensive fallback I/O.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-mode callers share _inFlightListSessions; stale epochs permit one shared trailing recomputation. Per-row fallback remains under Limiter(4), and provider prewarms are grouped by provider.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm catalog rows avoid provider/session-database fallback. Copilot metadata prewarm remains positively cached with TTL and shared in flight; small fallback sets remain on exact-session reads. Startup sampling stops after success or three attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: list coalescing, limiter, metric callback, storage counters, and completion placement were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large catalogs increase the added count pass linearly, but it is allocation-light and bounded to startup sampling; no evidence indicates material latency relative to the existing O(n) list and I/O work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new expensive boundary is added, concurrency remains bounded/coalesced, and the only collection-wide addition is a bounded lightweight pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Registration-time sessions_v2 migration and provider catalog backfill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing backfill-state database read determines whether provider enumeration is needed; required candidates are then resolved and persisted before migration completes. The diff observes the existing decision and report counters without issuing additional reads or scans.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the provider backfill marker and persist migration results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One backfill read per effective migration attempt; attempts are coalesced per provider, with a forced follow-up only when explicitly queued.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same backfill read and writes occurred; the new callback only receives the already-read boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing database work remains on migration completion and can indirectly gate an empty first listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate provider-native sessions through Copilot/Claude SDKs or Codex app-server thread/list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one scan per provider requiring migration; provider migration is single-flight, and explicit force requests queue at most the required fresh follow-up rather than fan out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider scans occurred before instrumentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing provider enumeration remains part of a required migration; deferred providers do not claim an empty catalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue bounded migration start/end telemetry through the existing telemetry pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three observed attempts per normalized provider/operation key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Migration emitted existing logs but no startupMark records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No telemetry flush is awaited; only local fixed-size event construction/enqueue occurs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective provider count and candidates returned by required provider scans; metrics reuse report totals rather than traversing imported candidates again.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration remains coalesced by provider in _ensureProviderCatalog. Candidate resolution retains its existing limits and ordering; telemetry does not schedule work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persistent backfilled marker skips enumeration on warm startup unless forced. Deferred/unavailable attempts remain distinguishable and sampled at most three times.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the migration callback is invoked immediately after the existing read, and report metrics are scalar fields.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider scan duration and candidate count vary widely, but those expensive operations predate the diff and are neither duplicated nor made more concurrent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: instrumentation reuses existing decisions and aggregate counters and does not alter boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claude, Codex, and Copilot discovery/catalog enumeration after startup or explicit provider use
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SDK availability checks precede existing provider enumeration. Codex pages thread/list and maps results; Claude and Copilot list once and classify results. Discovery generally runs after startup-settled or explicit activation and is off host bootstrap readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send thread/list requests to the Codex app-server process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing pagination up to THREAD_LIST_MAX_PAGES; the diff increments scalar page/session counters inside each existing response and adds no request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same thread/list pages were requested; repeated cursors already terminated, while the diff only labels that termination as truncated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests gate Codex discovery/migration results but not general host bootstrap readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call the Claude SDK session listing and map returned sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing SDK list per discovery/migration attempt, with discovery retry capped at three and provider startup timing independently capped at three observations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK list occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates Claude catalog publication, generally off bootstrap readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call the Copilot client listSessions method for migration, discovery, or threshold-triggered metadata prewarm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing SDK call per effective operation; metadata prewarm remains shared in flight and TTL-cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK call occurred; the diff wraps it with counters and timing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates the corresponding provider operation only; no telemetry-triggered scan exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read rollout prefixes for uncached candidate threads and maintain discovery watches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work proportional to uncached filtered Codex threads, with the existing limiter/cache; telemetry adds only counters before this mapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rollout/cache and watch behavior occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can gate Codex catalog mapping but is unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Provider-native session/page counts after existing pagination and filtering. Added work is constant per page plus constant per completed scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentService starts discovery once per provider; provider implementations retain existing retry/single-flight behavior. Codex list calls are coalesced by _codexChatList, and per-session classification/metadata reads remain under existing limiters.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Codex retains state-DB-only warm reads and metadata caching; Copilot retains metadata TTL/in-flight caching; successful startup observations stop further timing, while provider operation caches/retries are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: wrappers call each original availability/list API exactly once, and tests explicitly exercise no-extra-request behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native SDK and filesystem costs depend on catalog size, but changed lines do not increase their count, concurrency, or critical-path placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: boundary calls and cache semantics are preserved, with bounded scalar instrumentation only.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host shutdown with startup operations still in flight
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Shutdown disposes the startup recorder; any open timings are completed locally as cancelled. No shutdown path waits for telemetry delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue at most one cancellation marker for each bounded active operation key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by the fixed operation/provider key set; active entries are cleared immediately after completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No startup timing cancellation events existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No remote completion or flush is awaited during disposal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed operation/provider combinations, not user data or process lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disposal iterates a fixed, normalized key space and invalidates callbacks by clearing active state/maps.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All active state and pending bootstrap marks are cleared on disposal; late completions are ignored.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disposal and callback guards were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry appender enqueue cost is backend-dependent but bounded to a small fixed set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: cleanup is bounded and does not retain active timings or await I/O.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 30 changed files and all diff pages. Traced bootstrap, first-list, migration, provider discovery/prewarm, telemetry serialization, cache/coalescing, boundary fan-out, concurrency, and shutdown lifecycle. The PR adds bounded fixed-size telemetry and one startup-only count pass while reusing existing database/SDK/subprocess operations; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
